scope: Four pre-registered volatile official documentation or repository URLs; no source discovery was performed.

verified_claims: Sentence Transformers distinguishes asymmetric search, where a short query retrieves a longer corpus passage, from symmetric search.
Its current guide recommends encode_query for queries and encode_document for corpus entries in asymmetric retrieval.
The guide describes exact semantic_search usage for corpora up to about one million entries and notes that ANN can return results that are not exact.
records.boundary: The one-million-entry guidance, API names and performance recommendations are library-version guidance, not a capacity guarantee for every model, hardware or index configuration.

verified_claims: The pinned pgvector repository documents HNSW and IVFFlat index types for PostgreSQL vector search.
Its HNSW section states a better speed-recall trade-off than IVFFlat together with slower builds and greater memory use, and documents m, ef_construction and ef_search parameters.
The repository documents filtering, iterative scans, loading and index-maintenance topics as implementation concerns.
records.boundary: This is pgvector behavior at the pinned commit. Relative performance, memory use and filtering behavior must be measured with the chosen PostgreSQL version, data distribution and workload.

verified_claims: Qdrant documents HNSW vector indexes and Payload indexes as separate mechanisms.
Its indexing guide states that Payload indexes accelerate filtering on structured fields and high-cardinality metadata during similarity search.
records.boundary: The index selection and query-planning behavior are Qdrant product behavior; cardinality, memory and latency choices remain workload-specific.

verified_claims: The pinned Faiss repository describes the project as a library for efficient similarity search and clustering of dense vectors.
The repository exposes vector-index, approximate-search and GPU implementation material at the pinned revision.
records.boundary: Repository capability labels do not establish a production configuration or benchmark outcome. Algorithm, recall and hardware choices require task-specific evaluation.
